name: Adam Schiff (via Democrats.org)
subject: Trump wants me arrested...
body:
---
Derek, it’s Adam Schiff. Donald Trump has repeatedly called for me to be arrested for a variety of imagined offenses, including treason. All because I’ve stood up to him — as the manager of his first impeachment, on the January 6th Committee, and as a U.S. Senator. And like his attacks on universities, law firms, private companies, media organizations — you name it — he wants to try to silence any opposition or independent thought. **President Trump is hoping that threats of political retribution will intimidate those who have been brave enough to oppose him, but his attacks won’t stop me.** I will continue to fight against him and his MAGA cronies to preserve our freedom and democracy. I’m not backing down because I believe in the idea of America. Because I believe that we are capable of standing for freedom — not just at home but abroad. Because I believe that, at our core, we are a nation that takes care of its most vulnerable — not cuts their healthcare. I’m not alone in fighting back — **the DNC isn’t giving up either.** They’re investing _millions of dollars_ in local organizing and state parties. They’re taking on the Trump administration in court. They are doing the work to elect Democrats up and down the ballot who can act as a check on Trump’s power. **The DNC and I are fighting back because we think this fight is worth it.** We’re fighting back because we know that — even though it won’t be easy — this is a fight that we can win together. To do that, though, we need you to fight back too. **[Derek, if this struggle is important to you too, could you pitch in $3 to the DNC today to help them take on Republicans in 2025 and beyond? name: David Hogg
subject: It doesn’t have to be this way
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
CNN had me on to talk about what happened in Minnesota yesterday.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250828-2&t=1&akid=2591%2E587540%2Ey-pu0o)
Peter,
I am really tired of days like we had yesterday after the shooting in Minnesota. I’m not writing this to ask you for money, I’m just writing to say it doesn’t have to be this way. This is not an issue that we lack knowledge on how to solve. This is an issue that our elected officials lack the courage to address.
That’s why, live on CNN, I looked directly into the camera and reminded Donald Trump that after the Parkland shooting, he called out other elected officials and said they wouldn’t do anything because they were afraid of the NRA and he wasn’t. Then he met with the NRA and did nothing...because he is a coward.
As hard as these days are, I would like to remind you that the biggest obstacle to changing gun laws after Parkland wasn’t if it was actually possible, but that people didn’t think it would be possible. So many people told students after Parkland to give up because there was a Republican trifecta. But we were foolish enough to believe we could make change, so we showed up by the thousands to demand action at our state capital. As a result, we raised the age to buy a gun to 21 and passed a red flag law that has been used thousands of times in Florida. Then in 2022, Congress passed the first federal gun law in 30 years after the Buffalo and Uvalde shootings. Thousands of lives have been saved as a result of these laws, but you aren’t going to hear about the shootings that don’t happen. We have made and continue to make progress, even though it’s never fast enough.
Thank you for supporting Leaders We Deserve. A core part of why we do this is rooted in the fact that while older generations didn’t go through school shooter drills, they did go through nuclear bomb drills and when they grew up they passed the largest arms reduction treaties in human history. I believe progress was made because they knew the anxiety of what it was like to be told by your government the best it can do to hide you from a weapon of mass destruction is to shelter under a desk.
While I have little faith that the current cowards in power will successfully address this, I do have hope in the young people you all have enabled us to support in their elections. I have hope that just maybe one day, a generation going through school shooting drills will be history, not a constant headline.
Thank you,
David Hogg

clean_body: | | | | Hey friend, I joined NV Dems Chair Daniele Monroe-Moreno to talk with local NV Democrats about the chaos going on in Washington and what we can do about it. Trump and his Congressional Republican enablers are making a mess of things — driving up prices for everyday necessities from groceries to gas and taking money from working families to finance billionaire tax cuts. In my experience when it gets this bad in Washington, people are craving leadership that takes action for good and what Governors do at the state-level makes all the difference. Unfortunately for Nevada, Governor Joe Lombardo is one of Trump’s favorites. GOP Gov Lombardo “issued a record 162 vetoes” since taking office, including on policies that would have supported the middle class and expanded access to quality and affordable healthcare. Enough is enough — this stops with us. Opportunities to get engaged and support strong leadership in Indy | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/b76e94e544ce/the-wins-and-the-work-ahead-18251650?e=d9ebccf591)

| |
# UPCOMING EVENTS IN YOUR COMMUNITY
Friends,
In these difficult times for our city and our state, the need for strong leadership and even stronger communities is greater than ever. As your state senator, I've been working hard to protect our democracy from the dangerous and fiscally irresponsible proposals to call a special session on redistricting, but I also realize that the most powerful actions we can do are not at the state house, they're right here in our own communities.

That's why I'm asking you to **join me at a series of events throughout Indianapolis this month** : to help make sure that our state and our city have the strong leadership they need, and to make sure that our communities are ready to rise to whatever challenge they might face. If you've been wondering what you can do to make an impact in face of the often overwhelming national news, these can be a great opportunity to make a difference where it's felt most.
* I'll be hosting an **ice cream social at Shin Dig, on Wednesday, 9/10 from 5 to 7 pm,** where you can meet me and other Hoosiers passionate about making a change, and help contribute to my efforts to protect our communities. [RSVP here](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=97bc315f33&e=d9ebccf591).

* I'll also be at a **make and meet at Tuggle's Gifts & Goods on Monday, 9/15 from 6 to 7:30 pm**, where you can join me for an evening of civic creativity. We will decorate tote bags with patches, pins, stencils and more-- all while enjoying bubbly drinks, sweet treats, and great conversation. [Get tickets here](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=ccd0729daf&e=d9ebccf591).

* I'll also be at the Senate Democrat's **Save our State Concert, at the HI-FI Annex on Sunday, 9/28**. This all-ages show will be a high-energy concert to bring together all of of us who believe that Indiana can be better, and who are willing to fight for our state. [Get tickets here.](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=8846f3eeb5&e=d9ebccf591)

Check out the flyers below for more information about all these events!

Also, take a look below at all the exciting things I have been doing over the past few weeks: there's lots of work still to be done, but I am proud to be a part of the work that members of our community are doing to make our city the best it can be for all of its residents.

I hope to see you soon, Andrea

# SENATOR HUNLEY IN THE NEWS

**Democrats blast Indiana Republican lawmakers for White House visit amid redistricting push.**
[WFYI News](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=e4450c3033&e=d9ebccf591)

_Sen. Andrea Hunley (D-Indianapolis) called on Republican legislators to forgo pay if a special session is called.

"And at a time when our state budget is already crunched, this is so irresponsible to ask our taxpayers to foot the bill," Hunley said._

**Take a look inside the $69 million affordable housing project opening on Indy’s southside**
[Indy Star](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=bc722c3f85&e=d9ebccf591)

_Given the clear need for affordable housing in Indianapolis, State Sen. Andrea Hunley said it’s important for neighbors, like Bethany Lutheran Church, to welcome more affordable housing projects into their communities.

“When people see those orange signs, they say ‘Not in my backyard, oh my goodness, what’s happening?’” she said. “I think that what we need to remember at the end of the day is we’re creating opportunities for neighbors and we’re taking care of each other.” _

**See Indy's newest mural featuring Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton**
[Indy Star](https://andreahunley.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5c2b34b98b419cb5ca0511f25&id=2dbea1d104&e=d9ebccf591)
I had the privilege to speak at the unveiling of the latest "Keepers of the Culture" mural ahead of BUTTER: A Fine Art Fair, which will take place Aug. 28-31 at the Stutz. It was honor to meet the talented artist, William Minion, and to support projects like these that keep our communities together. Art has an important role to play in building identity and bringing vitality to our neighborhoods, and BUTTER does important work to keep that local art thriving.

name: Elise Stefanik
subject: I was ambushed by professional Far Left agitators
body:
I will not be intimidated by these stunts

| | | | |
---
Fellow patriot, they crossed the line.
I recently attended what should have been a peaceful and solemn memorial event in Plattsburgh, New York to honor the memory of a public servant. John Zurlo was a patriot who served his community in Upstate New York for decades.
An event meant to honor the memory of his service should have brought the community together but Far Left Democrat agitators had other plans and decided to crash the event.
**[A mob of Radical Democrats traveled to my district to ambush this non-partisan memorial in an attempt to intimidate me.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**
They were desperate to generate headlines.
Unfortunately, they got the attention that they cynically were after:

[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
They screeched, booed, and even called me a traitor...
These agitators have put a massive target on my back and coordinated efforts like this to smear me are only going to become more vicious and frequent in the weeks and months ahead.
**[I am in their crosshairs because I have vowed to Save New York from Kathy Hochul and New York Democrats by electing leaders in the Empire State that will RESTORE LAW AND ORDER.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**
I have seen the damage that Democrat’s insane open-border agenda and soft on crime policies have done to New York and our country.

**Failed Democrat leadership is destroying my home state and America along with it:**

* First, Hochul and Biden opened the floodgates at our southern border to our country.
* Then, crime has skyrocketed while Democrats handcuffed our law enforcement.
* Now, American families are suffering while our communities are being overrun.

It is clear that we are in the fight for the future of our nation.
But in order to undo the damage we need strong leadership. We need a Governor that will work with President Trump to clean up our streets.
**_[That’s why I am on the frontline to defeat Kathy Hochul and MAKE AMERICA SAFE AGAIN.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_**

[MAKE AMERICA SAFE AGAIN](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
I proudly stand with ICE and law enforcement, I support President Trump’s fight to secure our border, and I will not be intimidated into silence.
I am never going to stop fighting for my constituents and the American people but I need support to overcome the unhinged radicals that we are up against.
It is imperative that we answer this sham attack with strength and I need you to help send that message right now.
My team and I are pushing back against these attacks but they are well funded by Democrats who want to drown us in negative press to protect Kathy Hochul and prevent New York from becoming the next red state.
I plan on setting the record straight and I need more resources to combat their attacks on all fronts.
**_[So please, chip in $50, $25, or whatever you can today and fill out our donor survey to help me fight back](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_.**

[STAND WITH ELISE - FIGHT BACK](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
Friend, your support is so vital because I know that they aren’t going to stop with this event and they aren’t going to stop with me.
If we give them even an inch, they will come for every conservative voice and silence anyone who dissents.
_You_ know, _I_ know it, and _THEY_ know it too.
We cannot let that happen.
They have no respect for our laws or for our country. They think they can boo, harass, and scream us into silence.
I’ve got news for them:**_[we’re not going anywhere.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_**
Let’s answer back, together, by showing them that we will NEVER bend the knee.
I hope that you choose to continue to support our fight to restore the rule of Law in our nation and Save America.

_For America,_
[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
**Elise Stefanik**
[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/b4AT/?__vbtrk=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzE1MTk1OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)

[Consumer spending rose 1.6%](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMFutSAUhJ8Gdxg8AnoXLP6Nu_tvuzQoB6VBsXB6rW_f2PQNupvJJDP55u05Pm2IYV_-2w0N-TTueJaIRJhHnNOetmtCSwW_DpzJUkh78SMIUFz0HB6jsyFeo6yc8YiAbYWm6ZSWGhrQ1Wq8Ft55VKBU38xSPqS3XiFqq5SdZFMFc7eJHh6NEL1UddtB5-XcS6u7XrQTkwJdoJTr9xR2WtHHK70w13PaqmhWoqOw9h-DgcFwnmc9T-WmuHMGwy0ZDIs7-C8QX3I6aeXl9o5_fNpMmLm3hTAzGKps3HGGGEPRHZNi2WyIP2v0p4teBr4DAAD__5EUfIE), while a key measure of domestic demand—final sales to private domestic purchasers—climbed to 1.9%. On the import side, economists say some of the 2nd quarter growth was driven by companies accelerating their imports earlier in the year to beat tariffs, lowering costs this quarter. The third quarter is tracking near 2.2% so far.

| Friends-
Last month, the President signed H.R.1 (more commonly known as the Republican Congressional Budget or the 'Big Beautiful Bill') into law, and states have begun grappling with potential repercussions, particularly to Medicaid and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). These programs promote health care and food access, respectively, and together are essential for the well-being of youth and families.
Voices for Virginia's Children has reviewed H.R.1's lengthy text and highlighted key takeaways in various formats, including an [in-depth blog post](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ZjKwET4OWhHr05YEx557tKKO7bAl3D9PEq9z7Hre4DzeYHumWmSJ395cGGLc3jwQY92SKWMNeGZGG7McebG9PDU64KQOqhfdDbHO1yocrkOlyG61TvscKMLnVhIp3_8GiL0haa1Jpwk2r4OBJATazcArW6W5N0xFjyAcfJ8mfoD7lIqqpuYUa2pA7HX9Z5JeBMVqLaPL-9Rj2StnG9YwsQHTLM_GtDXN4qCJvO6WJX4cczH8FwyVeg==&c=Xrc37Ar0r1t8-xVeBaJz0uwToOwanWBw9TPoSZknViGeNjZlVy-JUQ==&ch=r3sFePQgz_SCPuFsvig3X7uusnKYOXeQzBXxACv6BGRbKKAtoZne5Q==), a [deep-dive policy memo](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ZjKwET4OWhHr05YEx557tKKO7bAl3D9PEq9z7Hre4DzeYHumWmSJ395cGGLc3jwQXGZj20vVUCDcHAoQi_5AbImbpg4W9yQCdwqZx4PbTsUBhv31suvozwa-fMAdLlnOEZhjGTSbeKp-T6Ov7P0KR9QJpe3vgaaQGwhMyPmOt9kVySrKFmAMDnFdh400YXFbFv1sz0dan7bsAdQekzVe5ncEcYrBedpmOGjiuaQg39p_U75jRskl66sUS3TH-hy0ywt-QybywTCcFHUgu5A_-w==&c=Xrc37Ar0r1t8-xVeBaJz0uwToOwanWBw9TPoSZknViGeNjZlVy-JUQ==&ch=r3sFePQgz_SCPuFsvig3X7uusnKYOXeQzBXxACv6BGRbKKAtoZne5Q==) sent to lawmakers, and a [Fireside Chat](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ZjKwET4OWhHr05YEx557tKKO7bAl3D9PEq9z7Hre4DzeYHumWmSJ395cGGLc3jwQACJt-fNAJ-PheY8SIpVYuYy3B_BMgL2rRjvDcwah0V444qUOM5DrNBzAvvMbK9QG9yRvr5CvZjt3tObv-6VVQvIAdTCi485I&c=Xrc37Ar0r1t8-xVeBaJz0uwToOwanWBw9TPoSZknViGeNjZlVy-JUQ==&ch=r3sFePQgz_SCPuFsvig3X7uusnKYOXeQzBXxACv6BGRbKKAtoZne5Q==) to address community questions and concerns. ## 'Bathroom Bill' Advances
The Texas House passed legislation yesterday that prohibits the use of a bathroom [designated for the opposite sex](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3u4yAQBfDT4I4I8EdCQZHG1WbbLa3BDDZaDBZM_o5vv3KusN1II_303vvzml4QYkjLb9jQ0MfnKeFRIxJhmezb2oh7hIRUVyzBeygFK01KqJ6LB1d6chDiOXWNM1Y4LRs08t4P3dArrZvVeKcetofZDsLZrpVWq6GFYbbYP4SWugnmwsRDaSmFbLvbfVDyPqNs3Wy9kMA6gS5QLjdakfAD1ccz_2C5zXlrolmJ9sraJ1MjU-NxHLetpuvH1IiJvytT41WKqfF7fwm-5ndFHlKgADGePP-tnAqkumByWLgFWkvOG7eQOHjCwk-EUnn2fMk7ByLcdrpAKPz5lL_Ka81NMW4_QoyhDnfWiWWDEL856f_W_THqXwAAAP__CtSR2g) in a government building. The Senate must approve changes to the bill before it goes to Gov. Greg Abbott. Senate Bill 8 was amended to [increase the penalty](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL-SpCAQxp8GM6aAUdSA4BKzvfRCq5FGqWrBgp7dnbe_cpN7gIu7v9_358_H-gGJUt5_w4mOv2NZM341Qmasq395T3gRZOR2YE0xQq3YeDXKDFJN0sxrgETvte-C8yrMukOnx8H2djDz3B0uPLWOU7TRG-8NwDQHiANuvfXWBoVdcjdMTWbWWuln_xit0eOG-hk2H5UG0SsMiUt98IGM39Aivcsn1sdWzo7cwXw18fwlzCLMsvkGr8Yp31dhlruOMAuVDUiY5Ucvj_JqKC9oDZv0wEct5ZQ-EUkuktKZWO63RT4xs4QcZNuOUujf8w3wb8kVctsxd9WF6ysRpWZH0av9hEQ_Afn_Zv105m8AAAD__84Ukbs) for a first-time offense from $5,000 to $25,000 and for subsequent offenses from $25,000 to $125,000. | Friends,

Tuesday marked four years since the Abbey Gate terrorist attack, a tragedy in which 13 brave American service members lost their lives.

They were part of the force that carried out the largest non-combatant evacuation in U.S. history. Their courage helped more than 120,000 people escape to safety, including over 80,000 Afghan allies. Because of their sacrifice, tens of thousands of Afghans now have the chance to begin new lives in the United States, free from the grip of the Taliban.

Tomorrow marks four years since the withdrawal from Afghanistan, the event that ended America’s longest war. This moment urges us to reflect not only on the closing of that chapter, but also on the immense sacrifices made over two decades by those who served.

2,459 American service members lost their lives, and countless others continue to bear visible and invisible wounds. As we remember this anniversary, we commit to honoring their courage, their devotion, and the heavy burden they carry for our nation.

---
| Letter from the Chair
---
What does the Nebraska Republican Party (NEGOP) do?
That's a question I hear often, especially when fundraising. Many people, myself included, like to give directly to candidates. But the Party plays an important role that individual candidates cannot fill on their own, and it needs support to carry out those responsibilities.
Last week, I attended my second Republican National Committee (RNC) meeting in Atlanta, where the 168 members elected a new Chairman, Joe Gruters, who was endorsed by President Trump. The "168" refers to the Chairman, Committeewoman, and Committeeman from each state, along with representatives from the District of Columbia and five U.S. territories. Former Chairman Michael Whatley will now be running for U.S. Senate in North Carolina.
One of the biggest benefits of attending an RNC meeting is seeing how important strong Republican organizations are at every level. The President himself is deeply engaged with the national Party and is, without question, our leader. Vice President JD Vance also spoke at the meeting, along with representatives of the President. These gatherings make it clear just how vital state parties are to the success of the national effort.
Here in Nebraska, the NEGOP is a key piece of that structure. When the State Party is organized and effective, it strengthens districts and counties, creating a unified political strategy. This structure is the foundation for maintaining the Party's brand and achieving electoral success.
What sets each state party apart? While the RNC develops a national platform, every state party creates its own. The national platform is presented and voted on every four years at the GOP Presidential Convention. Nebraska's platform will be reviewed, updated, and voted on in 2026. Both the national and state platforms outline Republican principles, policies, and priorities. They are meant to guide our candidates, and while they are aligned, each reflects the unique needs and priorities of its state.
Financially, the NEGOP is also able to support candidates in ways they cannot do on their own. This includes certain transfers and expenditures, especially for federal candidates, as well as funding shared initiatives like voter registration drives and get-out-the-vote efforts. Much of this work is funded through "party building" contributions rather than donations made to specific campaigns.
At the end of the day, the NEGOP is part of a much larger effort. We play our role in electing Republicans at every level, from federal races to local precincts. We are preparing, building, and working to strengthen our Party. When we work together, we win.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

# What's Happening...
---
From the legislative desk
On August 14th, the NEGOP convened a community roundtable in Scottsbluff focused on healthcare access and affordability. It brought together residents, healthcare providers, local leaders, and policymakers to address pressing challenges in our healthcare system, including Medicaid reforms included in the Big Beautiful Bill, and identify solutions to ensure access to affordable care. Panelists included Congressman Adrian Smith, State Senator Brian Hardin, Jessica Davies, Panhandle Public Health Director, Kent Ewing, Mayor of Gering, and Cory Morris, Heritage Estates Administrator. I was privileged to serve as moderator for the event.
Rising costs of prescriptions, insurance premiums, and out-of-pocket expenses were central concerns. Community members shared personal stories of financial strain and difficult choices between medical care and basic needs. Local panel members provided shared perspectives on operational challenges they each face and underscored the urgency of reform. Congressman Smith and Senator Hardin provided valuable insights into ongoing obstacles and legislative efforts to improve healthcare affordability, including additional reforms.
Several community members expressed their appreciation for the Congressman and Senator's commitment to listening and engaging with their concerns. Special thanks to Chairman Mary Jane Truemper, Kay Schroder, and Margaret Applegarth for their help with the event. Future roundtables are listed below, and you are encouraged to attend. Details will be included in the Chairman's newsletter as they get closer. Last week I attended my first RNC meeting in Atlanta. The meeting focused on party leadership transitions and strategic planning for the 2026 midterm elections. It was thrilling for me to be in the room to witness former RNC chair, Michael Whatley, pass the gavel to our new RNC Chair, Joe Gruters, after a unanimous election. There was a strong sense of party unity and excitement in the room.

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair What does the Nebraska Republican Party (NEGOP) do? That's a question I hear often, especially when fundraising. Many people, myself included, like to give directly to candidates. But the Party plays an important role that individual candidates cannot fill on their own, and it needs support to carry out those responsibilities. Last week, I attended my second Republican National Committee (RNC) meeting in Atlanta, where the 168 members elected a new Chairman, Joe Gruters, who was endorsed by President Trump. The "168" refers to the Chairman, Committeewoman, and Committeeman from each state, along with representatives from the District of Columbia and five U.S. territories. Former Chairman Michael Whatley will now be running for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. One of the biggest benefits of attending an RNC meeting is seeing how important strong Republican organizations are at every level. The President himself is deeply engaged with the national Party and is, without question, our leader. Vice President JD Vance also spoke at the meeting, along with representatives of the President. These gatherings make it clear just how vital state parties are to the success of the national effort. Here in Nebraska, the NEGOP is a key piece of that structure. When the State Party is organized and effective, it strengthens districts and counties, creating a unified political strategy. This structure is the foundation for maintaining the Party's brand and achieving electoral success. What sets each state party apart? While the RNC develops a national platform, every state party creates its own. The national platform is presented and voted on every four years at the GOP Presidential Convention. Nebraska's platform will be reviewed, updated, and voted on in 2026. Both the national and state platforms outline Republican principles, policies, and priorities. They are meant to guide our candidates, and while they are aligned, each reflects the unique needs and priorities of its state. Financially, the NEGOP is also able to support candidates in ways they cannot do on their own. This includes certain transfers and expenditures, especially for federal candidates, as well as funding shared initiatives like voter registration drives and get-out-the-vote efforts. Much of this work is funded through "party building" contributions rather than donations made to specific campaigns. At the end of the day, the NEGOP is part of a much larger effort. We play our role in electing Republicans at every level, from federal races to local precincts. We are preparing, building, and working to strengthen our Party. When we work together, we win. Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party | | | | What's Happening... From the legislative desk On August 14th, the NEGOP convened a community roundtable in Scottsbluff focused on healthcare access and affordability. It brought together residents, healthcare providers, local leaders, and policymakers to address pressing challenges in our healthcare system, including Medicaid reforms included in the Big Beautiful Bill, and identify solutions to ensure access to affordable care. Panelists included Congressman Adrian Smith, State Senator Brian Hardin, Jessica Davies, Panhandle Public Health Director, Kent Ewing, Mayor of Gering, and Cory Morris, Heritage Estates Administrator. I was privileged to serve as moderator for the event. Rising costs of prescriptions, insurance premiums, and out-of-pocket expenses were central concerns. Community members shared personal stories of financial strain and difficult choices between medical care and basic needs. Local panel members provided shared perspectives on operational challenges they each face and underscored the urgency of reform. Congressman Smith and Senator Hardin provided valuable insights into ongoing obstacles and legislative efforts to improve healthcare affordability, including additional reforms. Several community members expressed their appreciation for the Congressman and Senator's commitment to listening and engaging with their concerns. Special thanks to Chairman Mary Jane Truemper, Kay Schroder, and Margaret Applegarth for their help with the event. Future roundtables are listed below, and you are encouraged to attend. Details will be included in the Chairman's newsletter as they get closer. Last week I attended my first RNC meeting in Atlanta. The meeting focused on party leadership transitions and strategic planning for the 2026 midterm elections. It was thrilling for me to be in the room to witness former RNC chair, Michael Whatley, pass the gavel to our new RNC Chair, Joe Gruters, after a unanimous election. There was a strong sense of party unity and excitement in the room. Minnesota Bishop Robert Barron called Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey's criticism of prayer responses to the Catholic school shooting **["completely asinine,"](https://substack.com/redirect/b8718f59-20f4-43f7-a887-5edf3f981a4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Frey said "Don't say this is about 'thoughts and prayers' right now -- these kids were literally praying."

###
Property taxes are one of the most frustrating taxes Mississippians face, and they often rise quietly through something called the **millage rate**. Most homeowners don't think about millage until the tax bill shows up in the mailbox, but by then the decision has already been made and the money already spent.
A "mill" is one-thousandth of a dollar, applied to the assessed value of your home or land. In Mississippi, an owner-occupied home is assessed at 10% of its value. That means a $100,000 home is taxed on $10,000. If your county, city, and school district together charge 125 mills, your bill comes out to $1,250.
That's a lot of money for working families, retirees, and farmers. And here's the problem--too often, local boards quietly raise the millage rate instead of tightening their belts. It may not be called a "tax increase," but it has the same effect: families pay more while government grows.
Yes, we all want good schools, safe roads, and reliable services. But those things don't require endless tax hikes. What they require is **responsible leadership, disciplined spending, and respect for the fact that every tax dollar comes out of a family 's pocket first**. Raising millage should be the last resort, not the first solution.
Property taxes are unique because they never go away. You can pay off your home, but if you fall behind on property taxes, the government can still take it. That's why millage rates matter so much--they're about more than budgets, they're about protecting property rights and keeping our communities affordable.
Every supervisor, school board member, and city official should be asked one simple question before they vote to raise millage: **are you protecting taxpayers, or are you growing government?**
The people of Mississippi deserve leaders who put families first, live within their means, and treat every dollar with care. If we keep watch on millage rates, we can make sure government works for us--not the other way around.

| Peter— Trump’s henchmen showed up on our streets. At jobsites. In our neighborhoods. In early May, nearly 200 of our neighbors in South Nashville were rounded up in a sweeping ICE raid — a federal operation that had the blessing and cooperation of Bill Lee and Tennessee Republicans. They call it law and order. But here’s the truth: **📊 65% of people detained by ICE this year had no criminal convictions.
📊 93% had never been convicted of a violent offense.** ** ** Most of those detained are not and have never been threats to public safety. They are parents. They are workers. They are Tennesseans trying to build a better life for their families. This is what Trump’s assault on innocent immigrants looks like: indiscriminate arrests, no due process, shattered families, and fear flooding our communities — all while DHS admits it can only name _four_ people with criminal records out of the nearly 200 taken in Nashville. **The Tennessee House Democratic Caucus is fighting back.** We’ve introduced legislation to protect immigrant families, promote local control over policing, and ensure due process for every Tennessean — regardless of status. But we need your help. 👉 Can you chip in $10 to power our fight for humane, practical immigration policy?

you probably have a lot of unread emails, but I hope you’ll open his one
Peter, if your email inbox looks anything like mine, you’ve probably got a bunch of unopened emails from campaigns asking for help before the end-of-month this weekend.
So, yes, I know emails like this get to be pretty annoying. But I hope you’ll take a moment to let me explain why our campaign here in New Jersey really does need your support:
**1) We’re one of only two governor’s races that will be decided in 2025.** The election is just over two months away. “Fall short of our goal but hope to make up for it later” isn’t an option right now, Peter — because there is no “later” for us. Either we get the resources to get our message out on TV, online, and in person starting immediately, or we don’t.
**2) Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans are going to do everything they can to defeat me in this race.** Trump has already endorsed my opponent, Jack Ciattarelli, and led a rally for him — meaning MAGA money from all over the country is going to pour into Ciattarelli’s campaign. Not to mention, Ciattarelli’s being supported by a MAGA super PAC that’s pouring millions of dollars into negative ads that make one false assertion after another about my record and my character.
**3) Polls show what was already a close race getting even tighter.** Ciattarelli’s super PAC has been attacking me relentlessly for weeks, and it’s clearly having an impact, Peter. These polls also show that over 10% of voters are still undecided — so if we don’t get our message out to them before Ciattarelli does, losing doesn’t just become a risk. It becomes a likelihood.

On August 4, Rwanda’s parliament passed a groundbreaking new law that expands access to sexual and reproductive health care for adolescents. Thanks to this reform, young people aged 15 and above can now seek contraception, HIV prevention, and other essential care without parental consent—an urgently needed change that will help reduce teenage pregnancy and safeguard health and futures. The new law also establishes the country’s first framework for assisted reproductive technologies.

This victory is the direct result of years of work led by the Center for Reproductive Rights and partners. We engaged policymakers, amplified youth voices, and leveraged international human rights standards to drive reform. With your support, the Center is not only dismantling harmful barriers to care in Rwanda but also setting a powerful precedent for reproductive rights across the region.

**The Trump administration recently announced its plans to ban abortion care and counseling for veterans and their families—even in cases of rape, incest, or health emergencies.** This dangerous policy would block care for millions who access health care through the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and would only permit a narrow exception to save the life of a pregnant veteran. These kinds of exceptions to save a person's life often don't work in reality.

[**The VA is accepting public comments on this proposed change through September 3, 2025. This is our chance to speak out and stop it before it becomes law.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/114206836/566302790/1152959552?sourceid=1150868&utm_campaign=26emgfl-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0ODhjMjFmMy1kODg0LWYwMTEtYjQ4NC02MDQ1YmRlYjc0MTMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qTwGnYCHes3_SCLkQxXfKLrYAb-aOE9rN2qG-KDqlB4=&emci=0faed93b-ac82-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&emdi=488c21f3-d884-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&ceid=954237)

Personalized comments make a bigger impact. **The government may count identical submissions as just one, so we strongly encourage you to share your thoughts in your own words.** Need inspiration? You could write about:

body:
Republicans in Texas are currently redrawing the map for U.S. House districts to correct the congressional map that the Biden Department of Justice insisted on after the 2020 census. | [](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=93e8cf10b26b443f944d2f4e94b40d4e&_e=b6zMtZXji2N_0rXkn-5BxaDM4bjaMI4nmCoXzbD_t9_n8js6zhRx_THxSu7XFYSkDQ01avTpwXVaCuB68AAGGSa1yxOFNhcU0u94lxWa9H7-ghPrIOTD9JLvdNB2M7SnDYwPB-0noj0RqH2IR3CSJIOQnGaNf50dVCgNBsOcHEtX_-qYUR7DToBNF4uA-aUedun0ydvt0j1KQrzuB1Vr-vQNwqWTBeRGyj8Dr3Mzez_kacW80Tj5ihHfXgwJg8sh1BYeZemRXmTp-VmQc5lfDUDCx9RnOqNyzLUpdaeL7f0SQqbJbwS-6LvRneCuZfpXyr0-Zc9xDwosQr4tgrgoXN4JCjOVmNJRDDzX0R22I3eO_S-Uux_74--QudEc_YbRxEiIPC6P6PLFlhDKkXf4ps7YxR1drpG8X1QddVNjFqSW3_qNl8u_JfmkwBZwWBsdlQ7RFiPtEj_jowgooFC2dlo6pjdjqDcjVZQutY05W6BXRPaSWKILP29I8epQfuk3cobmueHyOUlGWT14Etl8Bsemd8Sr51kuZ-7Sgqeok3MfWhDF-K3j2GtRtouTVy-PJrnlXwXrm7HrpaV70Ok_aLZPU1pPElOBrB8XGr8h7CRpE_rA5f0twV3y0gYrmuNFc7SnbhQYOqtqpntM_QdZaj5OVYCDAaEPVfxjPUG9ZNpPwuxox_GrDBpN7feAINwbr094VHhbKLDbQiyy0GJUFbqb2zBZ0FLRz2rRPw65vbDs7LJFJ92nXejS50mZfGZAU7cKIwCepKcl092Ewf8vYg%3D%3D)

---
Peter,

_**I need you to read this carefully**_ — what’s happening with redistricting right now could reshape Congress for the next decade, and Democrats are doing everything they can to rig the game before the next election.

**After the 2020 Census** , Biden’s Department of Justice forced states like Texas to redraw their congressional districts to help Democrats. Now, under the Trump administration, the DOJ has reversed course — declaring those maps to be unconstitutional gerrymanders.

**Texas Republicans are taking action — redrawing the map in a special session, and the result could be up to 5 new GOP seats in the U.S. House.**

That’s why Democrats are panicking. **Gavin Newsom is already threatening to redraw California’s map in retaliation. body:
Join me in the fight.
#
Peter — North Carolina is a swing state, and we can be sure that Republicans will go all out to defeat us. But I know how to win North Carolina. _Whether it was Attorney General or Governor, I’ve done it over and over in the most competitive years._
It takes the dedication to connect with folks in every community, the commitment to fight for the rights that people hold dear, and the courage to stand up in the face of threats to the progress we’ve made.
**I served as Governor for eight years. I know that North Carolinians don’t want to go backward. And based on the enthusiasm we’re seeing for our campaign from people across our country, that sentiment is true for Americans everywhere.**
As a U.S. Senator, I will fight for our rights to the ballot box, reproductive health care, clean air and drinking water, and more. I will work to make health care _more_ affordable and accessible — not yank it away from those most in need. I’ll advocate for better public schools, more clean energy options, and opportunities for good-paying jobs. I will defend our democracy.
And I’ll never stop listening to what _the people_ need from me and meeting them where they are.
I believe that this is how you win a swing state, Peter. And I _know_ that — with you on our team — we can succeed here in North Carolina.

| | Hi Peter, Today is a day that weighs heavy on my heart. My daughter, Brooke, would have turned 10 years old. Brooke was born with Rett Syndrome, a rare neurological disease. We lost her when she was just five years old—but in those five years, she taught me more about courage, resilience, and love, than I could have ever imagined. Her life changed mine forever. It turned me from a lawyer and advocate into something even deeper—a mother fighting not just for her own child, but for every family facing impossible odds. That fight is what fuels me in this campaign. Because when we talk about healthcare, we aren’t talking about numbers on a page. We're talking about children like Brooke. We're talking about parents who just want their kids to have a chance, and families who deserve compassion and care—not barriers and bureaucracy. I can’t bring Brooke back. But I can fight for a Virginia where every family gets the care, dignity, and support they need. That’s how I honor her. If you’re able, I hope you’ll stand with me today. Together, we can build a future worthy of all our children.

| | Every single day since he took office in January, it seems like Donald Trump has found new ways to abuse his power and make life harder for our families. He's illegally withheld funding that New Jerseyans rely on for child care, for health care, and for access to healthy food. He's deployed the National Guard to American cities in a transparent attempt to instill terror and fear. He signed a devastating spending bill that guts Medicaid access and makes everything from groceries to heating your home less affordable — all to give billionaires a giant tax cut. And honestly, that's just a fraction of it. **As Trump has inflicted all this damage on our country, Republican politicians like Jack Ciattarelli have cheered him on every step of the way.** There is seemingly nothing Trump can do — no matter how illegal, reckless, or outright devastating for New Jersey families — that would make Jack Ciattarelli say "enough is enough." **And polls show that Ciattarelli is within a few percentage points of becoming New Jersey's next governor.** If we're going to win that race and prevent that from happening, we need to work night and day these next 10 weeks to get our message out. I intend to do exactly that — because the stakes for New Jersey, and for our nation, are too high to give it anything less. But I can't win this race without your help. name: Rudy Giuliani
subject: I’ve run out of time, resources, and options.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Rudy Giuliani Freedom Fund Legal Defense Trust
body:
My last chance. My Hail Mary.
| [](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=a21c69ce5e594e09a7831532d469eeaa&_e=GqA7a5cYG8FA_51X0fZ3w5apojyvG9AGkdsm2D9f8riVEGXXakfRVLgMSRba53Najx7D4F3PpDsITxd-IszsoWDZe0rRp1yZLm8nEJMAW5eLEC8Am2JdgBKaC5d-PjY5OE1Bqex4abWZPULXhIAUBqDMnEymccDslRqC2qq4bjLy5R1NHq2kdVByrSqhnFIBkF8vu_-9IYB2jVoLNV2T05JUR57_yrKa8rxc3Hkvno_9agU9cTKiusF9j_YFs7yf6usZ6Mc7KywsWFsGYqrGGNCw7ujGpuoGDshMJwS5y_wWSwd112TxNOtekHpWDHFkG-3tSQaEODm7Axni-0L1CpeB2fy6iAo-jW4yXY7d66o9nF5gfo-jcTNT6gZfa8SG3AR5_CKYzN7KtL6yhIRFIMG-Z6-Kj2aipuUT3zZcWe5MSFFhzS4fICLXn-hLH6PuYzWEjhci_HYZdYNi85MnKkbaVsomBstkgPwxuqT1mfmfDp0rxL9XCe5f-4mI5-utRF0OSP9XD76XRdmXUjCgTBFj9LFGWugJi0PJk5t6kXa9V0i6BmIDhM8FzZ6Xe_2WS9niK0SsBXnG6NQBtQsz0WYknOELb9UNoD1c6_X9pTtavy2HHhxOOY1pQQZzlKKk7iJP-TNIF1BO-IfGJ8gBWQ%3D%3D)
---
Friend,
---
Believe me, writing this letter was not my first choice...
---
_As a matter of fact, it’s my _last_ _resort_. _
---
**You see, I’m writing to you as a man who’s run out of time, resources, and options ahead of the TRIAL OF MY LIFE.**
---
**A Democrat Attorney General is making me stand in a rigged trial for bogus state-level crimes, because she knows that not even the most powerful man on the face of the planet – President Trump – can save me with a _federal_ pardon in _state_ court.**
---
And so, today, I’m not reaching out as America’s Mayor, not as a former prosecutor, not even as President Trump’s former attorney, but as a grandfather and a patriot who’s staring down a 20-year prison sentence for doing what I believed – _and KNOW_ – was RIGHT.
---
The Democrats and their Deep State goons think they’ve finally got me. They’ve left me with no escape, no lifeline – **especially after they’ve already STRIPPED me of my law licenses!**
---
_No viable pardon from the President.
No protection.
No cavalry coming over the hill.
_
---
But even though the most powerful man in the country legally cannot step in to save me, the most powerful _force_ absolutely can: _THE AMERICAN PEOPLE_.
---

I’m asking you to make a donation before our August fundraising deadline hits at midnight on Sunday.

In Arizona, we’ve got a slate of strong people running statewide. We’ve got excellent candidates for Congress. I’m doing whatever I can to help them out.

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Monday is Labor Day, the day each year that we recognize and celebrate the efforts of working men and women and of the American labor movement and its contributions to our lives. The labor movement has fought for protections that benefit all Americans — from the creation of the weekend and reasonable work weeks, to the expansion of health care coverage, to protections for children, to workplace safety. And it is leading today on many issues, advocating for members and nonmembers alike on issues that affect all American workers — fair pay, better health, secure futures, safe workplaces, constitutional rights, and democracy itself.
I have been proud to stand with the men and women of the labor movement throughout my time in Congress. And I am grateful to stand with them now as we fight for fair maps and full voices for Texans and all Americans. The right to organize and to advocate and to have a say in our government are central to our democracy. And we are all stronger when the voices of working Americans are heard. But these rights are under attack right now. From the White House to state houses to the Supreme Court, the victories the labor movement has fought so hard to achieve are facing new battles and new adversaries.
For generations, working Americans have not given up on the hope and the promise that American democracy and the American dream make possible. And I won’t, either. I remain committed to working to ensure that our rights are protected and our future is one of possibility and progress.
On Monday, remember all those who have worked for this progress. And I’ll join you in thinking of new ways that we can all carry on that work.
Together, we can do anything,

clean_body: ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [] Monday is Labor Day, the day each year that we recognize and celebrate the efforts of working men and women and of the American labor movement and its contributions to our lives. The labor movement has fought for protections that benefit all Americans — from the creation of the weekend and reasonable work weeks, to the expansion of health care coverage, to protections for children, to workplace safety. And it is leading today on many issues, advocating for members and nonmembers alike on issues that affect all American workers — fair pay, better health, secure futures, safe workplaces, constitutional rights, and democracy itself. I have been proud to stand with the men and women of the labor movement throughout my time in Congress. And I am grateful to stand with them now as we fight for fair maps and full voices for Texans and all Americans. The right to organize and to advocate and to have a say in our government are central to our democracy. And we are all stronger when the voices of working Americans are heard. But these rights are under attack right now. From the White House to state houses to the Supreme Court, the victories the labor movement has fought so hard to achieve are facing new battles and new adversaries. For generations, working Americans have not given up on the hope and the promise that American democracy and the American dream make possible. And I won’t, either. I remain committed to working to ensure that our rights are protected and our future is one of possibility and progress. On Monday, remember all those who have worked for this progress. And I’ll join you in thinking of new ways that we can all carry on that work. Hey friend,
We’ve had a very busy month. We finally had our County Chairs Brunch that we’ve been building towards, and it was a HUGE success.
Of course, this was all happening over the backdrop of Trump’s federal takeover of DC, the ongoing redistricting fight in Texas, and Trump’s planned executive order taking aim at mail-in voting. Now Trump is planning to deploy the Illinois National Guard to Chicago.

All of that to say, we know that the news is bad right now – but we also know that we cannot afford to give up our fight just because it’s getting difficult.

We can only make change if we have power – which we can only take if we win races for Congress, county board, city council, school board, and so many others. Our County Chairs know what it takes to win and it's our job to provide them with the resources they need to be successful.

Politico: Louisiana asks Supreme Court to gut Voting Rights Act and ban use of race in redistricting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=082925_1&amount=25]
There's no way to sugarcoat this, Team: Louisiana is asking the Supreme Court to gut the central provision of the Voting Rights Act and ban any use of race in redistricting.
In a legal brief filed this week, the state urged the Supreme Court to overturn a landmark 1986 ruling that established a legal test for when a voting map illegally dilutes minorities’ voter power. That ruling, Thornburg v. Gingles, has been understood for decades to require that states with significant communities of minority voters draw districts that fairly reflect their voting power.
Louisiana also told the Supreme Court it has made the decision not to defend the state’s current congressional map from 2024. That map contains two majority-Black districts among the state’s six House seats. This unusual move comes as the state claims it was " coerced " into complying with the Voting Rights Act.
This is exactly why the Supreme Court held this case over from last year. Chief Justice John Roberts has been working to gut the VRA for more than a decade. The VRA's provision against racial gerrymandering is one of the last major legs of the law standing.Just like the redistricting fights across the country, this is all about whether the party in power can choose their voters in order to stay in power in perpetuity.

| | | | | | Friend,
Our nation’s national debt is out of control. It recently surpassed $37 trillion and is growing around $2T a year. Our annual “Interest Only” payments now exceed $1T, surpassing America’s defense spending. Our country faces an existential crisis if Congress does not tackle out-of-control spending in Washington and make the necessary cuts.
Our problems are actually worse than that. Even as the strongest economy in the world, we struggle to sell our bonds and refinance our debt. To attract new lenders, we are forced to raise the rates we pay, increasing the interest expense of our debt. In a handful of years, we will be paying more than $2T a year in interest payments alone.
Every Republican campaigns as a fiscal conservative and promises to cut spending, but when they arrive in Congress, too many of them lack the backbone needed, and they vote with Democrats to spend, spend, and spend some more. I applauded President Trump and his efforts with DOGE, but even using their best-case scenario, the cuts were not going to be close to what we need to solve this problem. We need real growth, real cuts, and we need the discipline that would be forced on Congress by a Balanced Budget Amendment.
I voted for a federal balanced budget amendment when I served in the Arizona Legislature, and I will fight to pass one in the U.S. Congress. Bold conservative leadership is the only way to solve our nation’s debt problem and save the USA!

name: MassDems
subject: August Wins from Team Healey-Driscoll
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Peter,
August was a powerhouse month for Team Healey-Driscoll, delivering bold progress on housing, education, economic opportunity, and protecting patients' rights across the Commonwealth. From securing millions to expand preschool and career training, to advancing the West-East Rail project and strengthening legal safeguards for reproductive care, the Administration is getting results that matter. Here’s a look at just some of the impactful wins that are making life better for people across Massachusetts.
* On August 26, the Healey-Driscoll Administration’s Division of Insurance announced that five of the state’s health insurance carriers will return $75.6 million to over 350,000 people covered by individual and small employer plans in Massachusetts under the state’s enforcement of the Massachusetts health laws.
* On August 25, Healey-Driscoll Administration celebrated $3.5 million secured by the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) to continue advancing West-East Rail. This federal funding was awarded to the Rail and Transit Division, through the Federal Railroad Administration’s (FRA) Corridor Identification and Development Program (Corridor ID). It will be used to support the Boston-Albany Corridor Service Development Plan (SDP), which is an essential step in expanding and enhancing train service connecting Boston and Albany, New York, through Springfield.
* On August 25, Governor Maura Healey and Housing and Livable Communities Secretary Ed Augustus announced $15 million in Housing Development Inceptive Program (HDIP) awards to create 829 new homes in six Gateway Cities, which kicked off the program’s first funding round of 2025.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Maura%20Healey%20%231%20Aug%20Update%20.jpg]
* On August 21, Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that 30 school districts, in partnership with over 100 community-based preschool programs, will receive a total of $20.3 million in Commonwealth Preschool Partnership Initiative (CPPI) grants to expand access to high-quality, affordable preschool for children and families across Massachusetts. These grants maintain the state’s expanded access to high-quality preschool, supporting approximately 220 preschool classrooms and 3,200 seats for children across public schools, family child care, YMCAs, Head Start, and other community-based preschool programs.
* On August 21, the Healey-Driscoll Administration unveiled a 25-year plan to protect and restore nature across Massachusetts. The plan, known as the Biodiversity Conservation Goals for the Commonwealth, was designed to rebuild nature, sustain the health and well-being of residents, improve access to fresh food and enhance the overall quality of life and economy for everyone.
* On August 20, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced $290,000 in grant funding for four initiatives across Massachusetts to provide job training, employment placement, and post-placement services for 40 young adults with disabilities. As part of the grants, $77,500 will support planning grants for training providers.
* On August 20, the Healey-Driscoll Administration launched the Commercial Conversion Tax Credit Initiative (CCTCI), a new $10 million funding opportunity from the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (HLC) to help convert underused commercial buildings into residential and mixed-use housing across Massachusetts.
* On August 19, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced $1 million in grants to five organizations through the Executive Office of Economic Development’s Social Enterprise Capital Grant Program, which funds nonprofits focused on hiring and assisting people who face barriers to employment.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Maura%20Healey%20%232%20Aug%20Update%20.jpg]
* On August 19, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that it had approved 18 new career technical education (CTE) programs in 16 high schools. Together, these new programs will support 900 more students a year to access career-connected learning. These approvals include an aviation maintenance program at Greater Lawrence Regional Technical High School, the second such program in the state, at a time when the number of people employed in air transportation in Massachusetts has been increasing significantly and steadily.
* On August 19, Governor Maura Healey announced that 10 Massachusetts cities have received $5.7 million in funding to help ensure sufficient staffing for emergency services such as fire and police.
* On August 19, the Massachusetts Office of Travel and Tourism (MOTT) announced the 2024 economic impact of the state’s travel and tourism industry, which grew to $24.2 billion in direct spending from 52.6 million domestic and international travelers, generating $2.3 billion in state and local tax revenue and supporting 155,808 jobs across the state.
* On August 19, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that it was awarding $9.3 million in Partnership for Reading Success - Massachusetts (PRISM) II grants to 29 school districts and an educational collaborative. These grants are funded through Governor Healey’s Literacy Launch: Reading Success from Age 3 through Grade 3 initiative to make sure Massachusetts preschool programs, schools, educators and students have access to high-quality, evidence-based reading instruction.
* On August 14, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced the opening of the FY2026 round of the Seaport Economic Council Grant Program, which is administered by the Executive Office of Economic Development and provides funding to support working waterfronts, local tourism, coastal resiliency, and maritime innovation across Massachusetts’ coastal region.
* On August 13, Governor Maura Healey signed an Executive Order creating a Commission on Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) for State-Owned Land to advise her on potential reforms to the PILOT program. The state owns over half a million acres of land, such as state parks and forests, wildlife sanctuaries, beaches, and state military campgrounds. To compensate municipalities for the loss of local property taxes related to this land, the state administers a PILOT program that provides them with funding.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Maura%20Healey%20%233%20Aug%20Update%20.jpg]
* On August 13, the Healey-Driscoll Administration issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) for the redevelopment of a surplus, underutilized 5.05-acre parking lot located at 210 Springs Rd, Bedford on the Middlesex Community College Campus (MCC) into at least 20 new homes. This is the first RFP issued by the state since Governor Maura Healey launched her “State Land for Homes” initiative, an inventory of more than 450 acres of surplus state-owned land that could be used for the development of 3,500 new housing units across Massachusetts.
* On August 13, Healey-Driscoll Administration announced more than $2.3 million in new funding to expand ferry and water transportation services on the Boston Harbor. The grants will support six projects that make water-based transit a faster, more affordable, and more accessible option for residents — whether they’re commuting to work, visiting cultural landmarks or exploring educational opportunities along the harbor.
* On August 11, the Healey-Driscoll Administration declared August 10-16, 2025, as Urban Agriculture Week in Massachusetts, celebrating the innovation, impact and growth of farms in urban neighborhoods. To kick off the week, Lieutenant Governor Kim Driscoll and Massachusetts Department of Agricultural Resources (MDAR) Commissioner Ashley Randle visited Mack Park Farm in Salem, where they joined the local community for the farm’s annual Harvest Festival. The weeklong event will feature events across the state, highlighting the role urban farms play in delivering fresh, affordable food to city neighborhoods.
* On August 8, Governor Maura Healey signed into law a new Chapter 90 bill, delivering $300 million in critical transportation and infrastructure funding to every city and town across Massachusetts. The bill reflects the Healey-Driscoll Administration’s commitment to strengthening local roads, reducing congestion, and ensuring safe, reliable travel across the state.
* On August 7, Governor Maura Healey signed the updated Shield Law to strengthen protections for patients and providers. The new law prevents the disclosure of sensitive data, such as a physician’s name, and formally establishes that abortions are to be provided in emergencies due to medical necessity. Additionally, the law prohibits Massachusetts state or local authorities from cooperating with any federal or out-of-state investigation into health care services that are legally protected in Massachusetts, such as abortion care.
* On August 7, Massachusetts was ranked #1 in Outdoor Recreation Businesses Relocation. A recent report from Business Facilities, a leading resource for business site selection, ranked Massachusetts as the fastest-growing outdoor recreation economy. The outdoor recreation economy is a significant and growing contributor to the U.S. economy. It is also a growing factor in where businesses and employees alike decide to work and live.
* On August 6, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that it was awarding $3.3 million in Partnership for Reading Success – Massachusetts (PRISM) III literacy grants to 25 school districts and collaboratives. These grants will help school districts implement lasting improvements in English language arts and literacy instruction for grades 4–12 through the evaluation, selection and implementation of high-quality instructional materials.
* On August 6, one year after Governor Maura Healey signed the Affordable Homes Act (AHA) into law, the Healey-Driscoll Administration’s housing agenda is delivering results to increase the production of reasonably-priced housing and lower costs across the state. A new digital thermometer released by the administration today shows that since Governor Healey took office, more than 90,000 new housing units have been completed or are set to enter development.
* On August 5, Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that Massachusetts had officially met all state and federal licensure and certification milestones for its two state-operated veterans homes, signaling a new era of stability, oversight and excellence in care for those who served.
* On August 5, the Healey-Driscoll Administration awarded $24.2 million in Career Technical Initiative (CTI) implementation grants to 23 school districts to train 2,490 individuals for careers in high-demand occupations within the trades, construction, and manufacturing sectors across Massachusetts.
* On August 4, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that 272 schools in Massachusetts were selected to receive free, high-dosage early literacy tutoring this school year, designed to help students in kindergarten through third grade build foundational reading skills — with Grade 1 as the top priority. High-dosage tutoring provides one-on-one or small-group tutoring sessions multiple times a week for at least 10 weeks. This program was created by Governor Maura Healey as part of her comprehensive strategy to improve literacy for all Massachusetts students and is funded through a $25 million investment in Fair Share dollars.
* On August 1, Governor Maura Healey reminded Massachusetts renters, landlords and brokers that the state’s new policy banning forced renter-paid brokers fees goes into effect today. Earlier this year, Governor Healey proposed and then signed a provision in the Fiscal Year 2026 budget that prohibits landlords of residential rental properties from requiring that renters pay the landlords’ broker fees. Now, the broker’s fees for rental units must be paid by the person who hired the broker or salesperson.
*
August showed us what’s possible when bold leadership meets real action. Thanks to Team Healey-Driscoll, Massachusetts is not just making promises – we’re making progress. Whether it’s housing, education, infrastructure, or protecting fundamental rights, this administration is fighting for a Commonwealth that works for everyone. We’re just getting started.
Onward,
MassDems

On August 25, Governor Maura Healey and Housing and Livable Communities Secretary Ed Augustus announced $15 million in Housing Development Inceptive Program (HDIP) awards to create 829 new homes in six Gateway Cities, which kicked off the program’s first funding round of 2025. [] On August 21, Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that 30 school districts, in partnership with over 100 community-based preschool programs, will receive a total of $20.3 million in Commonwealth Preschool Partnership Initiative (CPPI) grants to expand access to high-quality, affordable preschool for children and families across Massachusetts. These grants maintain the state’s expanded access to high-quality preschool, supporting approximately 220 preschool classrooms and 3,200 seats for children across public schools, family child care, YMCAs, Head Start, and other community-based preschool programs. On August 21, the Healey-Driscoll Administration unveiled a 25-year plan to protect and restore nature across Massachusetts. The plan, known as the Biodiversity Conservation Goals for the Commonwealth, was designed to rebuild nature, sustain the health and well-being of residents, improve access to fresh food and enhance the overall quality of life and economy for everyone. On August 20, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced $290,000 in grant funding for four initiatives across Massachusetts to provide job training, employment placement, and post-placement services for 40 young adults with disabilities. As part of the grants, $77,500 will support planning grants for training providers. On August 20, the Healey-Driscoll Administration launched the Commercial Conversion Tax Credit Initiative (CCTCI), a new $10 million funding opportunity from the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (HLC) to help convert underused commercial buildings into residential and mixed-use housing across Massachusetts. On August 19, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced $1 million in grants to five organizations through the Executive Office of Economic Development’s Social Enterprise Capital Grant Program, which funds nonprofits focused on hiring and assisting people who face barriers to employment. [] On August 19, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that it had approved 18 new career technical education (CTE) programs in 16 high schools. Together, these new programs will support 900 more students a year to access career-connected learning. These approvals include an aviation maintenance program at Greater Lawrence Regional Technical High School, the second such program in the state, at a time when the number of people employed in air transportation in Massachusetts has been increasing significantly and steadily. On August 19, Governor Maura Healey announced that 10 Massachusetts cities have received $5.7 million in funding to help ensure sufficient staffing for emergency services such as fire and police. On August 19, the Massachusetts Office of Travel and Tourism (MOTT) announced the 2024 economic impact of the state’s travel and tourism industry, which grew to $24.2 billion in direct spending from 52.6 million domestic and international travelers, generating $2.3 billion in state and local tax revenue and supporting 155,808 jobs across the state. On August 19, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that it was awarding $9.3 million in Partnership for Reading Success - Massachusetts (PRISM) II grants to 29 school districts and an educational collaborative. These grants are funded through Governor Healey’s Literacy Launch: Reading Success from Age 3 through Grade 3 initiative to make sure Massachusetts preschool programs, schools, educators and students have access to high-quality, evidence-based reading instruction. On August 14, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced the opening of the FY2026 round of the Seaport Economic Council Grant Program, which is administered by the Executive Office of Economic Development and provides funding to support working waterfronts, local tourism, coastal resiliency, and maritime innovation across Massachusetts’ coastal region. On August 13, Governor Maura Healey signed an Executive Order creating a Commission on Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) for State-Owned Land to advise her on potential reforms to the PILOT program. The state owns over half a million acres of land, such as state parks and forests, wildlife sanctuaries, beaches, and state military campgrounds. To compensate municipalities for the loss of local property taxes related to this land, the state administers a PILOT program that provides them with funding. [] On August 13, the Healey-Driscoll Administration issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) for the redevelopment of a surplus, underutilized 5.05-acre parking lot located at 210 Springs Rd, Bedford on the Middlesex Community College Campus (MCC) into at least 20 new homes. This is the first RFP issued by the state since Governor Maura Healey launched her “State Land for Homes” initiative, an inventory of more than 450 acres of surplus state-owned land that could be used for the development of 3,500 new housing units across Massachusetts. On August 13, Healey-Driscoll Administration announced more than $2.3 million in new funding to expand ferry and water transportation services on the Boston Harbor. The grants will support six projects that make water-based transit a faster, more affordable, and more accessible option for residents — whether they’re commuting to work, visiting cultural landmarks or exploring educational opportunities along the harbor. On August 11, the Healey-Driscoll Administration declared August 10-16, 2025, as Urban Agriculture Week in Massachusetts, celebrating the innovation, impact and growth of farms in urban neighborhoods. To kick off the week, Lieutenant Governor Kim Driscoll and Massachusetts Department of Agricultural Resources (MDAR) Commissioner Ashley Randle visited Mack Park Farm in Salem, where they joined the local community for the farm’s annual Harvest Festival. The weeklong event will feature events across the state, highlighting the role urban farms play in delivering fresh, affordable food to city neighborhoods. On August 8, Governor Maura Healey signed into law a new Chapter 90 bill, delivering $300 million in critical transportation and infrastructure funding to every city and town across Massachusetts. The bill reflects the Healey-Driscoll Administration’s commitment to strengthening local roads, reducing congestion, and ensuring safe, reliable travel across the state. On August 7, Governor Maura Healey signed the updated Shield Law to strengthen protections for patients and providers. The new law prevents the disclosure of sensitive data, such as a physician’s name, and formally establishes that abortions are to be provided in emergencies due to medical necessity. Additionally, the law prohibits Massachusetts state or local authorities from cooperating with any federal or out-of-state investigation into health care services that are legally protected in Massachusetts, such as abortion care. On August 7, Massachusetts was ranked #1 in Outdoor Recreation Businesses Relocation. A recent report from Business Facilities, a leading resource for business site selection, ranked Massachusetts as the fastest-growing outdoor recreation economy. The outdoor recreation economy is a significant and growing contributor to the U.S. economy. It is also a growing factor in where businesses and employees alike decide to work and live. On August 6, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that it was awarding $3.3 million in Partnership for Reading Success – Massachusetts (PRISM) III literacy grants to 25 school districts and collaboratives. These grants will help school districts implement lasting improvements in English language arts and literacy instruction for grades 4–12 through the evaluation, selection and implementation of high-quality instructional materials. On August 6, one year after Governor Maura Healey signed the Affordable Homes Act (AHA) into law, the Healey-Driscoll Administration’s housing agenda is delivering results to increase the production of reasonably-priced housing and lower costs across the state. A new digital thermometer released by the administration today shows that since Governor Healey took office, more than 90,000 new housing units have been completed or are set to enter development. On August 5, Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that Massachusetts had officially met all state and federal licensure and certification milestones for its two state-operated veterans homes, signaling a new era of stability, oversight and excellence in care for those who served. On August 5, the Healey-Driscoll Administration awarded $24.2 million in Career Technical Initiative (CTI) implementation grants to 23 school districts to train 2,490 individuals for careers in high-demand occupations within the trades, construction, and manufacturing sectors across Massachusetts. On August 4, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced that 272 schools in Massachusetts were selected to receive free, high-dosage early literacy tutoring this school year, designed to help students in kindergarten through third grade build foundational reading skills — with Grade 1 as the top priority. High-dosage tutoring provides one-on-one or small-group tutoring sessions multiple times a week for at least 10 weeks. This program was created by Governor Maura Healey as part of her comprehensive strategy to improve literacy for all Massachusetts students and is funded through a $25 million investment in Fair Share dollars. On August 1, Governor Maura Healey reminded Massachusetts renters, landlords and brokers that the state’s new policy banning forced renter-paid brokers fees goes into effect today. Earlier this year, Governor Healey proposed and then signed a provision in the Fiscal Year 2026 budget that prohibits landlords of residential rental properties from requiring that renters pay the landlords’ broker fees. Now, the broker’s fees for rental units must be paid by the person who hired the broker or salesperson. * August showed us what’s possible when bold leadership meets real action. Thanks to Team Healey-Driscoll, Massachusetts is not just making promises – we’re making progress. Whether it’s housing, education, infrastructure, or protecting fundamental rights, this administration is fighting for a Commonwealth that works for everyone. We’re just getting started. body:
We've already shown what this coalition is capable of, and we can do it again. | | | Peter, Billionaires are making their move in the New York City mayoral race. Over the last week alone, disgraced former Governor **Andrew Cuomo’s super PAC has raised $1.26 million.** 1 They are _panicking_ about recent polls showing Zohran Mamdani maintaining his lead in the general election as he continues to connect with working class New Yorkers.2 Billionaires, real estate moguls, and power brokers are terrified by Zohran’s movement — terrified that they might finally have to pay their fair share — so they are uniting to try and stop us. Fellow Conservative,

_**“Asshole. Buffoon. Mofo. Wannabe Hitler. Gangster. Vile villain.”**_

Those are just a few words Rep. Jasmine Crockett used to describe President Trump. But let's be honest: those insults aren't just about him. They're about you. About me. About anyone who leans conservative, wears a uniform, or believes in this country's founding values.

They think we're backward. They believe we are in the way. And worst of all, they think we'll take it.

**As a former Navy SEAL Officer and Marine Corps veteran, I've faced far worse than name-calling. I've deployed to over 70 countries. I've led warriors into battle. I've endured life-threatening missions.** And the most important lesson I've learned? Quiet professionalism always wins the day.

That's why I'm running for U.S. Senate in Minnesota — not to yell or mock, but to**fight with discipline, humility, and relentless purpose.**

I didn't plan on entering politics. But the more I came home from deployment, the more I saw a Minnesota I didn't recognize. Tim Walz's lieutenant governor — the person I'm running against — isn't just radically out of step with our values; she embodies the same hard-left extremism that's trying to rewrite our entire society.

While Walz called for calm in 2020, she was preparing a lawsuit against the Minneapolis Police. As crime soared and businesses burned, she blamed the people trying to hold the line. These are the people in charge now — and they're not moderating.

**You can close this email and forget my name. Or you can help send the second Navy SEAL to the U.S. Senate — someone trained for chaos, unafraid of the fight, and grounded in service, not ego. **

Twenty-four years later, I still feel that calling. It's just a different kind of battlefield.

This won't be easy. Minnesota hasn't gone red in a presidential election since 1976. And I know I'm the underdog — just a regular guy from Minnesota who's been asked to do extraordinary things one more time. With your help, I know we can flip this Senate seat for the Republican Party - but that will require you getting involved TODAY. And you have a choice.

__ I've earned advanced degrees from Harvard and Johns Hopkins. I've trained in nuclear deterrence. I've worked across cultures, built teams under pressure, and led calmly when it mattered most.
