name: Kathryn Harvey
subject: It has always been about our children.
body:
Help me raise $3,000 by August 31.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/3c883d764635/kathryn-harvey-for-congresscampaign-kickoff-6421017?e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
|
---
| | Welcome to Keeping Up with Kathryn Harvey. A weekly digest covering South Carolina politics and opportunities for engagement and action in the Upstate.
---
| |
### You keep showing up, and I’m grateful.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| |
### It’s been a week, and if I’m honest I’ve never been so exhausted. I can’t stop thinking about the children in Minneapolis, Gaza, and right here at home in Spartanburg.
### We are failing our children, and more specifically our policy decisions and the elected officials making those decisions are failing them.
### Fighting for what you believe in day in and day out is a marathon not a sprint. And I’m grateful that you all keep showing up. From Greenville to Spartanburg and everywhere in between we have excellent candidates running up and down the ballot this year to ensure our children have a better future. You can get me to the finish line on November 4 by signing up to [knock doors](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=99c06615fe&e=edbde6c9b1), [call voters](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=4e7af6e4c5&e=edbde6c9b1), and [contributing now ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=e83af261d5&e=edbde6c9b1)to help me reach my end of month deadline. Thanks to you, we’re only $3,000 away from our August 31 goal.
---
| [Contribute to Kathryn](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=f0e7e6d3a0&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
| |
# Listen to my interview with Rep Neal Collins
---
| | South Carolina Rep. Neal Collins joins me for a candid conversation about what it really takes to serve in the State House. From town halls in Easley to hard-fought battles over education funding, healthcare, and senior care, Collins shares why he stays focused on local needs instead of chasing viral headlines. He opens up about the frustrations of wasted time on political theater, the growing polarization in Columbia, and the quiet but critical work that rarely makes the news. This episode also dives into redistricting, DACA occupational licensing, and why voter turnout in primaries matters more than most people realize. [**Listen Up!**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=2673fe09b3&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
| |
# Knock doors with me on Saturdays & Sundays
---
| | Join me every Saturday at 10am & Sunday at 3pm for a neighborhood canvass to support my race for Spartanburg County Council! You can register to volunteer at the link below. Interested in phone banking for my campaign this Fall? Join us the third Thursday evening of each month for a virtual phone bank training! This is a great opportunity to volunteer on your own time and help my race for County Council. Register at the link below and you'll [receive a link to make calls. ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=d4ad8c453a&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
[|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=2abe5972df&e=edbde6c9b1)
| [Knock doors with me ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=cab813efc9&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| |
# SPCDP Monthly Meeting September 8
---
| | **Join us at the Spartanburg Community College Downtown Campus Theater at 220 East Kennedy Street on September 8 for our monthly meeting in our news space** as we hear from a panel of elected officials and strategists around the state on how we can strengthen our party. The remainder of our 2025 meetings will be held at this location September 8 | October 6 | November 10 | December 1.
---
[|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=b06cf1acc8&e=edbde6c9b1)
|
---
| |
# SC Sister Senators at Wofford Sept 29
---
| | Join us for the second installment of “Candid Conversations” an effort to bring together leadership from across the isle to foster civil discourse in today’s political climate. Hosted by the President’s Office at Wofford College, the SC Sister Senators who bridged together to fight for women’s rights in South Carolina, will join us for a special panel session moderated by the Honorable Rita Allison and a screening of their new documentary film trailer on September 29 at 6pm at Wofford.
---
|
---
| |
****Canvass with Kathryn Harvey every Sunday at 3pm**[**RSVP Here**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=584c8e2681&e=edbde6c9b1)****** **September 8: SPCDP Monthly meeting at SCC Downtown Campus****September 29: Evening with SC Sister Senators at Wofford College** October 21 - 31 Early Voting for the 2025 General Election 8:30 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. daily (Closed Saturday and Sunday), County Administration Building.**November 4: 2025 General Election (7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.)**
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Local News:**
* [**Former Congressman Trey Gowdy's comment following Minnesota mass shooting draws criticism**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=cffec5b1f0&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**Filing opens August 29 for two state legislature seats in the Upstate**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=92a8e2ebef&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**Group calls on City of Spartanburg to implement Hate Crimes Ordinance**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a2c0c41c1b&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**Groups rally to stop youth violence in Spartanburg**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=9115b1c70d&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**It's Rhyne in a landslide to win Spartanburg County Sheriff's race**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=9f33c43bdf&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**Spartanburg races for mayor, city council draw challengers, while 4 run for City Council 2 empty seat vacated by Rob Rain.**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=44bc927111&e=edbde6c9b1)[****](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=6de62dadb3&e=edbde6c9b1)

---
|
---
| | | | **National News**
* [**White house defends CDC Firing**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=1821f4491d&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**Judges poke holes in Trump’s DC Federal Intervention**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=8f24c6f7fb&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**Trump to end Vice President Harris’s Secret Service**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=6218894858&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [**SC GOP Governor hopeful clamour to show Trump ties**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=1c8b36b5d7&e=edbde6c9b1)

---
| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | This past week I attended the Greenville Dems monthly meeting with Dr. Annie Andrews and former GCDP Chair Amanda McDougald Scott, and Councilwoman Lillian Brock Flemming to talk about our races. Thanks to everyone who showed up and has already signed up to volunteer for local races in Greenville and Spartanburg!
I also had the pleasure of hosting a social media and communications training session for other local county party chairs during our meeting in Columbia last weekend with my friend and content creator [Anthony Milian](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a094d1b915&e=edbde6c9b1). Democracy is a participatory experience, join me at [kathrynforcouncil.com](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=2387dae3a0&e=edbde6c9b1).

name: Wes Moore
subject: A personal note from me about this end-of-month deadline
body:

Derek,
6 years ago, Trump made the phone call that forever altered the lives of me and my twin brother.
On July 25, 2019, my brother, Alexander Vindman, listened as President Trump attempted to extort our ally, Ukraine, by withholding military aid unless President Zelenskyy investigated Joe Biden.
At the time, I was serving as the senior ethics official at the National Security Council in the White House. After Alex reported the call to me, my brother and I made the fateful decision to do our patriotic duty and stand up to Donald Trump at the risk of our decades-long military careers.
We blew the whistle on him and reported his corrupt phone call with Ukraine up the chain of command. Our actions eventually led to his impeachment, and Trump retaliated by firing us from our posts.
The decision to blow the whistle on Donald Trump cost my brother and me our military careers. But over two decades ago, I swore an oath to protect our country and our Constitution from threats, foreign and domestic, and I would not let Trump deter me from that duty.
I ran for Congress last year to fight back against Trump and the far-right Republicans who enable his abuse of power and attacks on our Democracy.
I’ve done everything in my power to hold Trump and his MAGA cronies accountable — no matter the political cost — because I’ll never stop defending truth, democracy, and working Americans. But speaking out comes with consequences.
I’m already one of the GOP’s top targets in the House, and National Republicans have already dumped millions into ads smearing and attacking me. Republicans have made it clear that they’ll spare no resources in kicking me out of Congress, and it’s only going to get worse from here.
So today, I am asking you to support my campaign so I can continue defending our democracy and fighting for you in Congress.
**[Can you please split $10 between my campaign for Congress and Adam Schiff today? Colorado absorbed 43,000 illegal immigrants in 2 years as taxpayers foot the bill
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Friday!
🎙️ Check out today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A Pew report shows the state [absorbed 43,000 illegal immigrants in two years](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), costing Denver over $100 million. In Jefferson County, [officials may shut down Et Voilà!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), a Christian-run bakery, over zoning tied to the family’s trailers—sparking backlash from supporters. At CSU, students say Turning Point USA’s upcoming [Charlie Kirk event](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) is a rare chance for conservatives to debate openly and build community.
At the Capitol, lawmakers gave Governor Polis authority to [cut $300 million ](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)to address a [$783 million budget gap](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). The NRA Hunters’ Leadership Forum weighed in on how [disastrous wolf reintroduction has been](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), draining millions in depredation costs and forcing lethal removals. Meanwhile, Colorado’s leftward shift and rapid growth are [fueling resentment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in neighboring states.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** The New York Times faces criticism for a [hit piece on Riley Gaines](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), accused of smearing her while ignoring fairness in women’s sports, despite strong public backing for protections. At the same time, grim details continue to surface from the Minneapolis Catholic school shooting: attacker Robin Westman, a transgender individual, [left a manifesto](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) expressing regret over transitioning, violent fantasies, and threats against Trump before killing two students and wounding 17. Polis and Trump [ordered flags to half-staff](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to honor the victims.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** A new study warns of [disparities in domestic violence protection orders](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and questions the push for one-size-fits-all gun laws based on data models. Pastor Drake Hunter reflects on [lessons from Taylor Swift, Rocky, and The Wizard of Oz](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), urging balance between grief and joy to rediscover resilience. And C. J. Garbo argues the media is covering up the shooter’s anti-Trump motive, [downplaying violence against conservatives](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) while amplifying it when progressives are targeted.
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, August 29, 2025.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado absorbed 43,000 illegal immigrants in 2 years as taxpayers foot the bill](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [BREITBART](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
The estimated number of illegal aliens living in Colorado jumped from 160,000 in 2021 to more than 200,000 by 2023, according to the latest report by Pew Research Center. The largest number of those illegals ended up in and around Denver, the paper reported.
The number has jumped even more in the years covered by the Pew report, according to the Denver News Gazette. The paper noted that city officials pegged the number of illegals entering Denver at 43,000, of which about 20,000 have remained living in the city.
The Gazette also claimed that the influx of illegals has cost the taxpayers of the city of Denver at least $100 million. The Democrats’ orchestrated inflow of illegals has imposed massive civic costs on Colorado’s citizens, including higher taxes, lower wages, overcrowded schools, as well as more crime and chaos.

|

**[Colorado Lawmakers Hand Polis Authority for $300 Million in Spending Cuts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado lawmakers ended their special session by giving Governor Polis authority to [cut up to $300 million in spending](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to help close the state’s $783 million budget gap.
* Democrats already reduced corporate tax breaks during the session and expect further cuts will draw from state reserves and programs, though no areas are guaranteed protection.
* Republicans warn cuts may target Medicaid provider rates, affecting 1.2 million Coloradans, while Polis blames federal tax policies and says his team will try to minimize harm to schools, roads, and health care.

**[Swift, Rocky, and Oz: What Stories Teach Us About Being Human](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY DRAKE HUNTER, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Yesterday morning’s Today show lineup truly felt like it was straight out of a movie, with the charming romance between Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift (Sincerely, CONGRATULATIONS!), a heartfelt nod to Rocky’s classic resilience (my go-to movie), and a stunning reimagining of The Wizard of Oz at The Sphere in Las Vegas (the four characters I highlight when teaching temperament). But then, suddenly, came a jarring headline about shots fired at Annunciation Catholic Church, a place of worship and community (an understanding of “Annunciation” follows this piece)._
_The incident, which resulted in [2 deaths & 17 injuries as of this writing], shook us to our core and reminded us of the fragility of life. From glitz to grief in the span of a single news cycle. That’s our reality._
_The simple answer might be to lean towards cynicism, thinking “everything is falling apart,” or to escape into more celebrities and spectacle. But honestly, neither truly reflects how we feel._

**[When Violence Targets Conservatives, the Media Looks Away](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 29** _The nation is reeling after the tragic shooting at a Minneapolis Catholic school. Two children are dead, more than a dozen are injured, and the community is shattered. Investigators have identified the shooter as Robin M. Westman, and disturbing evidence has already surfaced: weapons scrawled with political messages, including “Kill Donald Trump."_
__

**[From silence to the mic: Why young conservatives say CSU’s TPUSA event matters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | AUGUST 28** _Turning Point USA is bringing Charlie Kirk and the American Comeback Tour to Colorado State University (CSU) on Sept. 18. The chapter will host two events that day—a midday “Prove Me Wrong” debate session and an evening program at the Lory Student Center Ballrooms. Doors open at 5:30 p.m., with priority seating for CSU students, though community members are also welcome. Registration is required and first come, first served._
__

**[The special session leaves Polis with a $783M deficit — here’s how he can fix it without new taxes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY RUSS MINARY | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 28** _Governor Polis recently called—and lawmakers have now concluded—a special session aimed at addressing the estimated State budget deficit of $1.2 to 1.6 BILLION. That means that every man, woman and child in CO has to pay $208 more this year. That’s in addition to all of the other current local, county, state, sales and special district taxes they are already paying. But kids don’t pay taxes; adults do. I think CO taxpayers and citizens already pay enough in taxes._

This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, August 29, 2025. – Team RMV | TODAY'S TOP STORIES The estimated number of illegal aliens living in Colorado jumped from 160,000 in 2021 to more than 200,000 by 2023, according to the latest report by Pew Research Center. The largest number of those illegals ended up in and around Denver, the paper reported. The number has jumped even more in the years covered by the Pew report, according to the Denver News Gazette. The paper noted that city officials pegged the number of illegals entering Denver at 43,000, of which about 20,000 have remained living in the city. The Gazette also claimed that the influx of illegals has cost the taxpayers of the city of Denver at least $100 million. The Democrats’ orchestrated inflow of illegals has imposed massive civic costs on Colorado’s citizens, including higher taxes, lower wages, overcrowded schools, as well as more crime and chaos. | Colorado lawmakers ended their special session by giving Governor Polis authority to to help close the state’s $783 million budget gap. Democrats already reduced corporate tax breaks during the session and expect further cuts will draw from state reserves and programs, though no areas are guaranteed protection. Republicans warn cuts may target Medicaid provider rates, affecting 1.2 million Coloradans, while Polis blames federal tax policies and says his team will try to minimize harm to schools, roads, and health care. | The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support! | BY DRAKE HUNTER, Yesterday morning’s Today show lineup truly felt like it was straight out of a movie, with the charming romance between Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift (Sincerely, CONGRATULATIONS!), a heartfelt nod to Rocky’s classic resilience (my go-to movie), and a stunning reimagining of The Wizard of Oz at The Sphere in Las Vegas (the four characters I highlight when teaching temperament). But then, suddenly, came a jarring headline about shots fired at Annunciation Catholic Church, a place of worship and community (an understanding of “Annunciation” follows this piece). The incident, which resulted in [2 deaths & 17 injuries as of this writing], shook us to our core and reminded us of the fragility of life. From glitz to grief in the span of a single news cycle. That’s our reality. The simple answer might be to lean towards cynicism, thinking “everything is falling apart,” or to escape into more celebrities and spectacle. But honestly, neither truly reflects how we feel. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 29 The nation is reeling after the tragic shooting at a Minneapolis Catholic school. Two children are dead, more than a dozen are injured, and the community is shattered. Investigators have identified the shooter as Robin M. Westman, and disturbing evidence has already surfaced: weapons scrawled with political messages, including “Kill Donald Trump." JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | AUGUST 28 Turning Point USA is bringing Charlie Kirk and the American Comeback Tour to Colorado State University (CSU) on Sept. 18. The chapter will host two events that day—a midday “Prove Me Wrong” debate session and an evening program at the Lory Student Center Ballrooms. Doors open at 5:30 p.m., with priority seating for CSU students, though community members are also welcome. Registration is required and first come, first served. RUSS MINARY | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 28 Governor Polis recently called—and lawmakers have now concluded—a special session aimed at addressing the estimated State budget deficit of $1.2 to 1.6 BILLION. That means that every man, woman and child in CO has to pay $208 more this year. That’s in addition to all of the other current local, county, state, sales and special district taxes they are already paying. But kids don’t pay taxes; adults do. ## New York is cooked...
I went to New York City to ask Zohran Mamdani supporters which of his policies do they actually think will work to make the city better.
* **Rent freezes**
* **Raising taxes on the rich**
* **Government-run grocery stores**

body:
Missouri voters deserve better than being used as pieces in Trump’s chess game. **BREAKING: Missouri House Democrat leaders expect Governor Mike Kehoe to call them back next week for special session**

_"Talks about redistricting in Missouri began at the beginning of the month. President Donald Trump appeared to weigh in last week."_ Peter,

Governor Mike Kehoe is expected to call a special session that could reopen Missouri’s congressional maps, and we know exactly who benefits if Republicans get their way: _Donald Trump and his MAGA allies._

This isn’t about fair representation, **it’s about rigging the game.**

Republicans want to follow Texas’s lead, slice up our communities, and gerrymander Missouri so Democrats barely have a fighting chance in one of eight districts.

Redistricting is supposed to happen once every decade, and it’s already been done. **But Republicans see an opportunity to twist the rules and rig the maps to their advantage so they can squeeze out more GOP seats.**

Our communities, our representation, and our democracy are not political bargaining chips for the GOP to use whenever they want. But the truth is, if they succeed, _it's Missouri voters who are going to pay the price for their reckless, self-serving games._

But Peter, we have the power to fight back, but first, we need to ensure we don't fall short of our end-of-month fundraising goal for August. Chris is New Hampshire through and through.
From helping run his family’s small business to serving in local government and in Congress, he’s always put our communities first — working to lower prescription drug costs, strengthen care for our veterans, and defend reproductive freedom.
Now he’s stepping up to run for the Senate at a time when our state and our country need his steady, values-driven leadership more than ever.
Meanwhile Scott Brown is back — and once again he’s counting on Republican mega donors and corporate special interests to try to buy a New Hampshire seat. We’ve seen this play before. He doesn’t represent our values, and we can’t let him take this seat.

Chris can win, but he can’t do it alone. He needs all of us with him, starting now.

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Ashli Babbitt Awarded Full Military Funeral Honors
body:
Fani Willis Scandal Update

[INSIDE JW]

AIR FORCE GRANTS FUNERAL HONORS TO ASHLI BABBITT

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76306&L=35984&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dWJlLmNvbS9saXZlL0JneEZBb09YWVhZP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=e97d14f197665c85afdfc95746b6cad935cbf731b810ebcb8de7ada14ce9332c]

We are delighted that the U.S. Air Force has finally decided to
provide full military funeral honors to Ashli Babbitt, the Air Force
veteran who was shot and killed inside the U.S. Capitol by
then-Capitol Police Lt. Michael Byrd on January 6, 2021.

We have been deeply involved in this case on multiple fronts from the
beginning.

Babbitt was the only official January 6 homicide victim. The Biden
administration had previously denied Babbitt and her family these
honors in retaliation for her being at the U.S. Capitol that day. This
new decision comes on the heels of a massive, nearly $5 million Trump
administration settlement to her family for wrongful death and other
claims against the U.S. Government.

Babbitt, 35, owned and operated a successful pool business with her
husband Aaron. Ashli traveled alone from San Diego to Washington, DC,
to attend the Women for America First (aka Save America) rally on
January 6, 2021, at the Ellipse near the White House.

On July 23, 2025, Judicial Watch Senior Counsel Robert Sticht wrote a
letter
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76306&L=35963&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2hlZ3NldGgtYmFiYml0dC1sZXR0ZXItMjAyNS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=3c2643870cf1ac571aaf39c6e99ddc28410d0ea8208bc2f16d1267fe6e20e48a]
to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth asking him to reverse the
“grave national injustice” of denying Babbitt and her family
military funeral honors:

> I am writing to urge you to make a new determination granting
> military funeral honors for SrA Ashli Elizabeth Pamatian, aka Ashli
> Elizabeth McEntee, and Ashli Elizabeth Babbitt, a War on Terror
> veteran of the U.S. Air Force and Air National Guard.

***

> I respectfully encourage the Department of Defense to favorably
> consider two major recent developments and also Ashli's lengthy and
> meritorious military service.

> First, on January 20, 2025, President Trump granted clemency for
> certain offenses relating to the events at or near the United States
> Capitol on January 6, 2021. The Presidential proclamation states,
> “This proclamation ends a grave national injustice that has been
> perpetrated upon the American people over the last four years and
> begins a process of national reconciliation.” President Trump (a)
> commuted the sentences of certain individuals convicted of offenses
> related to events that occurred at or near the U.S. Capitol on
> January 6, 2021; (b) granted a full, complete and unconditional
> pardon to all other individuals convicted of [similar]
> offenses....

> Second ... on July 2, 2025, the United States of America paid a
> damage award of nearly five million dollars to settle a wrongful
> death lawsuit that Judicial Watch and I brought forward on behalf of
> the Estate of Ashli Babbitt and her husband Aaron Babbitt to ensure
> justice and accountability for the fatal shooting of Ashli Babbitt
> on January 6, 2021. Once again, Gen. Kelly's denial of military
> funeral honors for Ashli's funeral cannot be reconciled with this
> landmark legal settlement. Many well-documented facts now clearly
> show that the fatal shooting was not justified.

> For example, Ashli was the only official homicide on January 6,
> 2021. Ashli, age 35, was unarmed when she was fatally shot. She
> stood 5’3’ tall and weighed 115 pounds. Her hands were up in the
> air, empty, and in plain view of Lt. Byrd and four armed officers
> behind him. Seven additional armed officers were behind Ashli,
> including four Containment and Emergency Response Team officers.
> Ashli posed no threat to the safety of any officer nor any Member of
> Congress who stayed after Member evacuation. Ashli was begging
> officers to call for backup before she was shot. Officers ignored
> Ashli. The only shot fired that day was the one Lt. Byrd fired to
> kill Ashli. Lt. Byrd was not in uniform. Lt. Byrd did not identify
> himself as a police officer or otherwise make his presence known to
> Ashli. Lt. Byrd also did not give Ashli any warnings or commands
> before firing the shot that killed her. Ashli never saw Lt. Byrd
> because he was hidden from her view. She was ambushed and
> defenseless. Multiple witnesses at the scene yelled, “you just
> murdered her.” Lt. Byrd later told the world on NBC Nightly News
> that he “had no clue” about the individual he shot. “I didn't
> even know it was a female until hours, way later ... that night,”
> he said.

***

> Ashli Babbitt's patriotic and courageous service in the U.S. Air
> Force and Air National Guard also merits favorable action on this
> request.

The decision to finally extend military funeral honors was confirmed
in a letter
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76306&L=35963&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2hlZ3NldGgtYmFiYml0dC1sZXR0ZXItMjAyNS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=3c2643870cf1ac571aaf39c6e99ddc28410d0ea8208bc2f16d1267fe6e20e48a]
on August 15, 2025, written by Under Secretary of the Air Force
Matthew L. Lohmeier to Aaron Babbitt, Ashli’s husband, and Ashli
Babbitt’s mother, Michelle Witthoeft:

> On behalf of the Secretary of the Air Force, I write to extend the
> offer for Military Funeral Honors for SrA Ashli Babbitt. I
> understand that the family’s initial request was denied by Air
> Force leadership in a letter dated February 9, 2021. However, after
> reviewing the circumstances of Ashli’s death, and considering the
> information that has come forward since then, I am persuaded that
> the previous determination was incorrect.

Ashli Babbitt’s family is grateful to President Trump, Secretary
Hegseth and Under Secretary Lohmeier for reversing the Biden Defense
Department’s cruel decision to deny Ashli funeral honors as a
distinguished veteran of the Air Force. Our team spent years
investigating, litigating, and exposing the truth about Ashli’s
homicide. We are proud to have done our part in bringing her family a
measure of justice and accountability for Ashli’s outrageous
killing. And our battle for justice will continue.

We obtained

Here’s how they judge our candidates — and how that process is broken:
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250829-1&t=1&akid=2600%2E587540%2EpXfY7p)
Hey, it’s Ben Young — I help recruit and support candidates at Leaders We Deserve.
Here’s something you won’t hear in public: When quarterly fundraising reports come out, DC insiders _obsess_ over them. They look at those numbers and decide — often without ever meeting the candidate or even researching them — who’s “viable” and who’s not.
That’s backward. That’s how we end up with the same types of politicians — wealthy, connected, cautious — while the status quo continues to fail the rest of us.
But here's the thing: When we help a candidate raise money the _right_ way — through grassroots support — it not only funds their campaign, it opens doors. It gets other organizations and donors to pay attention. It helps _build_ their operation and name ID.
We’re not just trying to elect people who already raise a ton of money — we’re helping young leaders _build_ power from the ground up. But to do that, we’ve got to hit our own goals first.

America’s strength comes from its families, whether parents work full-time, stay home with their children or find a balance somewhere in between. But for the millions of parents who want to return to work or need to do so after their children are born, the lack of affordable, accessible child care is a major barrier. It’s not just a personal challenge for individuals; it’s an obstacle that hurts the U.S. economy and dampens productivity, and it’s one we are decades overdue in addressing.

I know firsthand the challenges that working parents face because I’ve lived it. Fifteen years ago, before I was elected to the U.S. Senate, my husband and I searched for child care for our two children and struggled with the same challenges that other families still face today: long waitlists and scarce options. When we finally found a center that could take both of our children, we were shocked by the exorbitant cost. Signing those checks, we felt like we were paying for college tuition.

On Wednesday, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) criticized the blowback from Democrats over President Donald Trump's efforts to decrease rampant crime in Washington, D.C.

Earlier this month, Trump activated the National Guard and placed the DC Metropolitan Police Department under direct federal control to "reestablish law and order of public safety" in the nation's capital, which has been met with criticism from the left.

Britt told JT Nyeswander on "Alabama's Morning News" that Democrats being opposed to Trump's efforts to shore up the crime problem proved the party lacked common sense and was "embracing crime." She went on to say that safe streets were "imperative" for a better pathway to the American Dream for citizens.

clean_body: | | | | | | | America’s strength comes from its families, whether parents work full-time, stay home with their children or find a balance somewhere in between. But for the millions of parents who want to return to work or need to do so after their children are born, the lack of affordable, accessible child care is a major barrier. It’s not just a personal challenge for individuals; it’s an obstacle that hurts the U.S. economy and dampens productivity, and it’s one we are decades overdue in addressing. I know firsthand the challenges that working parents face because I’ve lived it. Fifteen years ago, before I was elected to the U.S. Senate, my husband and I searched for child care for our two children and struggled with the same challenges that other families still face today: long waitlists and scarce options. When we finally found a center that could take both of our children, we were shocked by the exorbitant cost. Signing those checks, we felt like we were paying for college tuition. | | On Wednesday, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) criticized the blowback from Democrats over President Donald Trump's efforts to decrease rampant crime in Washington, D.C. Earlier this month, Trump activated the National Guard and placed the DC Metropolitan Police Department under direct federal control to "reestablish law and order of public safety" in the nation's capital, which has been met with criticism from the left. Britt told JT Nyeswander on "Alabama's Morning News" that Democrats being opposed to Trump's efforts to shore up the crime problem proved the party lacked common sense and was "embracing crime." She went on to say that safe streets were "imperative" for a better pathway to the American Dream for citizens. | | U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, signed onto a letter sent to U.S. Department of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last Thursday, urging Lutnick to help address illegal Chinese fishing vessels. The letter, signed by Britt and U.S. Senator Rick Scott, R-Florida, alleged that fishers from China—the largest exporter of seafood to the U.S.—are engaging in illegal, unreported and unregulated, IUU, fishing at the cost of the U.S. seafood industry. | | | | | | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and proud to stand for every corner of Alabama—our cities, small towns, and rural communities alike. I’m rooted in faith, built on family, and committed to making Alabama stronger and better for generations to come. Alabama is a place of hard work, strong values, and unyielding independence. But the Left is trying to tear that all down. I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for every Alabamian who feels forgotten and left behind. Whether it’s securing our borders, protecting our children, or defending our way of life, I’m here fighting for Alabama’s future. This fight isn’t easy, but it's worth it. And I’m not going anywhere. _New Poll Shows Hoosiers Against Republican Attempt to Gerrymander Indiana Mid-Decade_
__ New polling released this week by Change Research shows 52% of Hoosiers are opposed to the GOP plot to cheat voters and redraw the maps mid-decade. This is yet another sign that every day Hoosiers are opposed to this blatant power grab by the Republican supermajority. That number rises to 60% opposed when folks learn more. In a time where polarization is so high, few issues bring together Hoosiers across the aisle like this cheating plot. ****_Republican Lawmakers Travel to DC to be Bullied by Donald Trump and JD Vance on Gerrymandering_
Around 50 state Republican lawmakers travelled over 600 miles away to Washington D.C. this week to be bullied by Donald Trump and JD Vance about cheating to gerrymander Indiana’s congressional maps mid-decade. Democrats held them accountable with a “Saynora Sellouts” gathering at the Indianapolis International Airport on Tuesday morning. It’s clear that Republicans are willing to do anything to cheat and gerrymander our state so that the voters are not in control. It’s time that we had leadership at the state level that put Indiana before Washington D.C. every time. This current Republican supermajority needs a wake up call from Hoosiers. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks._ This week, we are shouting out the amazing work of our Democratic state legislators who have stood with Hoosier families against the record utility bill increases throughout our state. Rep. Cherrish Pryor, Rep. Carey Hamilton, Sen. JD Ford, and other state lawmakers attended recent events to speak out to regulators against these absurd rate increases. The average family has seen their utility bills rise by 17.5% this year alone. clean_body: | Welcome to the Indiana Democratic Party's weekly newsletter, The Kernel of Truth. The State Party will provide the most important facts - a kernel of truth - from the week. = ** New Poll Shows Hoosiers Against Republican Attempt to Gerrymander Indiana Mid-Decade New polling released this week by Change Research shows 52% of Hoosiers are opposed to the GOP plot to cheat voters and redraw the maps mid-decade. This is yet another sign that every day Hoosiers are opposed to this blatant power grab by the Republican supermajority. That number rises to 60% opposed when folks learn more. In a time where polarization is so high, few issues bring together Hoosiers across the aisle like this cheating plot. Republican Lawmakers Travel to DC to be Bullied by Donald Trump and JD Vance on Gerrymandering Around 50 state Republican lawmakers travelled over 600 miles away to Washington D.C. this week to be bullied by Donald Trump and JD Vance about cheating to gerrymander Indiana’s congressional maps mid-decade. Democrats held them accountable with a “Saynora Sellouts” gathering at the Indianapolis International Airport on Tuesday morning. It’s clear that Republicans are willing to do anything to cheat and gerrymander our state so that the voters are not in control. It’s time that we had leadership at the state level that put Indiana before Washington D.C. every time. This current Republican supermajority needs a wake up call from Hoosiers. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. This week, we are shouting out the amazing work of our Democratic state legislators who have stood with Hoosier families against the record utility bill increases throughout our state. Rep. Cherrish Pryor, Rep. Carey Hamilton, Sen. JD Ford, and other state lawmakers attended recent events to speak out to regulators against these absurd rate increases. The average family has seen their utility bills rise by 17.5% this year alone. This is solely on the backs of the Republican supermajority who have given massive tax breaks to electric companies and allowed them to pass on the costs to consumers for experimental technology. Information on County Party events, Town Halls, protests, volunteer opportunities, and more can be found on our Make Your Voice Heard! IDOE – The Indiana Department of Education is taking its first round of feedback on a plan to reassign A-F ratings to all Indiana schools. body:
I love to cook.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=4112%2E400544%2Ew4HmkN)
Hey – it’s Deb.
One thing you should know about me is that **I love to cook.**
My love of cooking New Mexican cuisine started early, thanks to the hours I spent watching my grandmother bake bread in her mud oven and stir huge pots of posole. She wouldn’t let us kids in the kitchen while she cooked, but I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours. I still hold those memories close as I prepare my favorite traditional New Mexican dishes.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250829_2_posole?amount=5&refcode=em20250829-4112&refcode2=4112_400544_w4HmkN&akid=4112%2E400544%2Ew4HmkN)
_New Mexico chile – the best in the world!_
**There’s something powerful about connecting with others over a home cooked meal.** When I was in law school at UNM, I’d make chicken green chile stew for student gatherings, and I made that same dish for my Congressional colleagues during the 2019 winter holiday season. I even cooked chile and tortillas for the water protectors when I traveled to Standing Rock during the protests against the Dakota Access Pipeline.
Cooking became more than a hobby after I decided to start my own salsa business. I worked out of a commercial kitchen and bought my red chile pequin from a farm in northern New Mexico. I’d prepare my salsa and deliver jars to mom-and-pop shops across the state, often with Somáh riding with me in the back seat.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250829_2_posole?amount=5&refcode=em20250829-4112&refcode2=4112_400544_w4HmkN&akid=4112%2E400544%2Ew4HmkN)
_Here’s Somáh posing with jars of my homemade salsa. Kids in New Mexico start early... 🌶️_
**For me, cooking has always been a way to foster connection and build community, which is exactly what we’re doing now as we grow our campaign for New Mexico.** I’ve had the chance to sit down with New Mexicans in living rooms and at kitchen tables to hear about their lives, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. Every conversation is another reminder of the incredibly high stakes in this race – and proof that if we organize around our shared values, we will win.
[**Will you donate $5 before our major end-of-month deadline THIS Sunday, August 31st, to power our grassroots campaign? If you donate through this link, I’ll even send you my recipe for green chile chicken posole!**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250829_2_posole?amount=5&refcode=em20250829-4112&refcode2=4112_400544_w4HmkN&akid=4112%2E400544%2Ew4HmkN)
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250829_2_posole?amount=5&refcode=em20250829-4112&refcode2=4112_400544_w4HmkN&akid=4112%2E400544%2Ew4HmkN)**
Happy cooking,
Deb 🌶️
P.S. Throughout my life, cooking has helped me bring my community together – and bringing people together is exactly how we’ll win this campaign. [**If you make a donation of any amount through this link, I’ll be sure to send you my recipe for green chile chicken posole so you can cook it for your friends and family.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250829_2_posole?amount=5&refcode=em20250829-4112&refcode2=4112_400544_w4HmkN&akid=4112%2E400544%2Ew4HmkN)

Cooking became more than a hobby after I decided to start my own salsa business. I worked out of a commercial kitchen and bought my red chile pequin from a farm in northern New Mexico. I’d prepare my salsa and deliver jars to mom-and-pop shops across the state, often with Somáh riding with me in the back seat. Here’s Somáh posing with jars of my homemade salsa. Kids in New Mexico start early... 🌶️ For me, cooking has always been a way to foster connection and build community, which is exactly what we’re doing now as we grow our campaign for New Mexico. I’ve had the chance to sit down with New Mexicans in living rooms and at kitchen tables to hear about their lives, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. Every conversation is another reminder of the incredibly high stakes in this race – and proof that if we organize around our shared values, we will win. Happy cooking, Deb 🌶️ P.S. Throughout my life, cooking has helped me bring my community together – and bringing people together is exactly how we’ll win this campaign.
